title: Van Hollen Accuses Schumer Team of Using 'Fear' to Retain Senate Control, Demands Probe into Nvidia Security Scandal
snippet: Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen calls for fresh leadership in the Senate Democratic caucus while pressing for answers on a high-stakes national security breach involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
content:
WASHINGTON — Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen threw down the gauntlet on Sunday in his bid to become Senate Majority Leader, accusing long-standing Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer’s camp of using scare tactics and misinformation to hold onto power.

Appearing on ABC’s "This Week," Van Hollen argued that the American electorate voted against Donald Trump in the recent midterms but emphasized that Democrats cannot afford a return to "business as usual." He urged his colleagues to embrace internal reform as Democrats prepare to take control of the Senate in January.

'How About a Little Democracy?'

"I think there's a very open lane here. The Schumer team's put out a lot of misinformation," Van Hollen told host Martha Raddatz. "They're essentially trying to instill fear in people who may say that they're going to support me as a new leader... We just had a great day for our democracy around the country. How about a little democracy in the Senate Democratic Caucus?"

Schumer, who has maintained a firm grip on caucus leadership for years, countered on social media that while he welcomes discussions regarding the party's direction, he already possesses the votes required to maintain his role as leader. Nevertheless, Van Hollen insisted that voters expect the incoming Democratic majority to actively earn public trust rather than rely on the status quo.

Escalating Alarm Over Nvidia National Security Breach

Beyond intra-party leadership squabbles, Van Hollen—a key member of both the Senate Foreign Relations and Banking Committees—focused sharply on the unfolding national security scandal surrounding semiconductor giant Nvidia.

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following revelations of an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who is suspected of operating as a Chinese intelligence asset. Megaspeed has been under federal investigation since 2024 for allegedly smuggling Nvidia’s most advanced microchips into China in violation of U.S. export restrictions.

Van Hollen highlighted the grave national security risks of high-end technology falling into Beijing's hands, suggesting the illicit relationship may have facilitated illicit chip diversions. He further rebuffed claims by Donald Trump that the White House was unaware of the security threat before Huang accompanied Trump on an official trip to China in May.

"This is a president who lies to the American public all the time, and this is why we need an investigation. We need people testifying," Van Hollen stated. "I do believe he was briefed. I think all the information that I've seen suggests that this would not have escaped the attention of the president of the United States."
